name: qtads
why: An interpreter for TADS interactive fiction, an old-school environment worth a look despite being deprecated.

brief.what_it_is: QTads is a cross-platform, multimedia interpreter for TADS interactive fiction games. It takes compiled Tads game files for the Tads virtual machine and runs them on Linux, macOS, or Windows, with a Qt-based interface. It supports both Tads 2 and Tads 3 games, and the homepage says it is fully compatible with HTML TADS (Multimedia TADS). The GitHub README says it could in principle run on any system where Qt exists, but Linux, macOS, and Windows are the main targets.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a multimedia-capable player for TADS games, the Text Adventure Development System, a C-like object-oriented language for authoring interactive fiction. The README describes Tads as similar to Infocom or Legend Entertainment games like Zork.
brief.how_it_works: QTads does not implement the virtual machine from scratch. It builds on Mike Roberts' reference implementations of the T2 and T3 Tads VMs and adds the graphical, multimedia front end. The README says the Tads compiler produces executables for the Tads VM, and QTads runs those programs.

commands_seen.context: Gentoo install command quoted on the homepage for Portage-based distros. The page adds that non-~arch users may need to keyword the package in package.keywords to get the latest version.

brief.install_notes: Linux builds are self-contained AppImages and need no unusual external dependencies, and they should work on distributions as old as Ubuntu 18.04. Downloads exist for Linux x86-64, x86, ARM64 and ARM32v7, Windows 7 or later in 32-bit and 64-bit, and macOS 10.13 or later, with a separate legacy build for macOS 10.9 to 10.12. Source is available, and Gentoo users can install it from Portage. The GitHub README points to an INSTALL file and a manual page (qtads.6.gz), which I did not fetch. No accounts or first-run configuration were mentioned. Games are not included; the homepage points to the Interactive Fiction Archive and IFDB for finding them.
brief.standout: Most other interpreters that handle TADS, such as Gargoyle, Spatterlight, Zoom and FrobTADS, run TADS games in text-only mode. QTads is one of the few free options that plays Multimedia TADS games with their graphics and sound features.
brief.status: Quiet, not abandoned. The homepage lists version 3.4 as the current release, dated 2023-05-17, and the README copyright runs through 2023. I found no commit history or deprecation notice. The release is over two years old as of my reading, so updates have slowed.
brief.caveats: The scout note calls QTads deprecated, but neither the homepage nor the README says that, so treat the claim as unverified. The homepage describes it as current. Other caveats: the README says it targets Linux, macOS and Windows and only theoretically runs elsewhere; the Linux AppImages need Ubuntu 18.04 or newer; the source build process was not checked because I did not open the INSTALL file. The project is GPL v3 or later.
quotes: QTads is a cross-platform, multimedia interpreter for TADS games.
It is fully compatible with HTML TADS (aka 'Multimedia TADS.')
QTads is not written from scratch; it uses Mike Roberts' reference implementations of the Tads VM.
fetch_log: https://github.com/realnc/qtads - worked, README returned (overview only; INSTALL, NEWS and qtads.6.gz were referenced but not fetched)

judge.reason: QTads opens a niche interactive-fiction world, and its support for TADS graphics and sound sets it apart from text-only interpreters.

entry.title: QTads
entry.tldr: A graphical interpreter that plays TADS interactive fiction games, including the Multimedia TADS ones with pictures and sound that text-only players skip.
entry.deeper_look:
QTads runs compiled game files for TADS, the Text Adventure Development System. TADS is a C-like, object-oriented language for writing interactive fiction, the parser-driven genre of Infocom and Legend Entertainment games like Zork. QTads plays both Tads 2 and Tads 3 games with a Qt-based interface on Linux, macOS and Windows.

It does not reimplement the virtual machine. The project says it "is not written from scratch; it uses Mike Roberts' reference implementations of the Tads VM." The TADS compiler turns a game's source into a program for that VM, and QTads runs the program and adds the graphical and multimedia front end.

The door here is interactive fiction itself. A game is a program in a language built around objects, rooms and a parser that turns typed sentences into actions. Playing a few games shows what the genre can do, and TADS is also a language you can write in yourself.

QTads ships no games. The homepage points to the Interactive Fiction Archive and IFDB for finding them.
entry.install:
brew install qtads
# Homebrew marks this formula deprecated. The homepage also offers AppImages for Linux, and Windows and macOS builds.
# You need a TADS game file (.gam or .t3) to play; none are included.

try_this.what_happens: Opens the QTads window, where you can open a TADS game file you downloaded from IFDB or the IF Archive.

entry.whats_unique: Gargoyle, Spatterlight, Zoom and FrobTADS run TADS games in text-only mode. QTads is one of the few free interpreters that plays Multimedia TADS games with their graphics and sound.
entry.caveats: Homebrew marks the formula deprecated, though the homepage still lists 3.4 (May 2023) as current, so updates have slowed.
